subject.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove

question: After the atomic deletion defect is repaired, should OpenClaw adopt this experimental Claws status/remove lifecycle and ownership model as part of the open RFC stack?
rationale: The patch establishes destructive core CLI behavior, persisted provenance semantics, and partial-removal recovery contracts before the RFC or prerequisite branches are on main, so repository intent cannot be inferred from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Approve after atomic repair
options.body: Keep the plan-first status/remove design, require same-object verified deletion, and review the prerequisite stack in order.

options.title: Land status separately
options.body: Accept read-only status first and defer destructive removal until its filesystem and ownership contracts are settled.

options.title: Pause the Claws stack
options.body: Keep the drafts unmerged or close the series if maintainers do not want this lifecycle surface in core.

recommendation.title: Approve after atomic repair
recommendation.body: Keep the plan-first status/remove design, require same-object verified deletion, and review the prerequisite stack in order.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main fs-safe boundary and protected core product direction make this the strongest available decision route.
